entries.title: C0041 exact target and uncertain current openness
entries.statement: For a nearest-neighbor RWRE on Z^d, d>=2, sample once and retain an iid field of transition rows. Assume every allowed transition is at least a fixed kappa>0 almost surely. For a fixed unit direction ell, P_0(X_n dot ell -> +infinity)=1 is conjectured to imply P_0(liminf_n (X_n dot ell)/n>0)=1. Current openness UNKNOWN: a September 2026 primary repository claims a solution; this packet does not verify that claim and does not solve the target.
entries.domain: probability, random walks in random environments

entries.title: Balanced inward-row density pattern for finite boxes
entries.statement: B(x,r)=x+[-r,r]^d intersect Z^d, r an integer >=1; L=2r+1; n_r=r(2r+1)^(d-1); b_1(y)=omega(y,+e_1)-omega(y,-e_1). For delta>0, I_delta(x,r) counts rows in B with y_1<x_1 and b_1(y)>=delta, plus rows with y_1>x_1 and b_1(y)<=-delta. The plane y_1=x_1 is ignored. A_delta,theta(x,r)={I_delta(x,r)>=2 theta n_r}, theta in (1/2,1]. D(theta||1/2)=theta log(2theta)+(1-theta)log(2(1-theta)), with 0 log 0=0.
entries.domain: probability, random walks in random environments

entries.title: Draft finite-box exit moment bound under uniform ellipticity
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED SPECIAL-CASE CLAIM. In any nearest-neighbor environment on Z^d with every transition at least kappa>0, iid is unnecessary. Let B=x+[-r,r]^d intersect Z^d, r>=1 integer, L=2r+1, p=kappa^L, and T_B be first exit. Uniformly over z in B, P_{z,omega}(T_B>mL)<=(1-p)^m, E_{z,omega}T_B<=L/p, and E_{z,omega}(T_B^s)<=M_r(s)=2^s s! L^s kappa^(-sL) for every integer s>=1.
entries.domain: probability, random walks in random environments

entries.title: Draft entropy bound for inward-oriented row density
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED SPECIAL-CASE CLAIM. B(x,r)=x+[-r,r]^d intersect Z^d, r an integer >=1; L=2r+1; n_r=r(2r+1)^(d-1); b_1(y)=omega(y,+e_1)-omega(y,-e_1). For delta>0, I_delta(x,r) counts rows in B with y_1<x_1 and b_1(y)>=delta, plus rows with y_1>x_1 and b_1(y)<=-delta. The plane y_1=x_1 is ignored. A_delta,theta(x,r)={I_delta(x,r)>=2 theta n_r}, theta in (1/2,1]. D(theta||1/2)=theta log(2theta)+(1-theta)log(2(1-theta)), with 0 log 0=0. If environment rows are iid, P_env(A_delta,theta(x,r))<=exp(-2n_r D(theta||1/2)). At theta=1 this is at most 4^(-n_r). Combining this with uniform ellipticity, for each fixed theta>1/2, kappa>0 and integer s>=1, sum_{r>=1} 2^s s! (2r+1)^s kappa^(-s(2r+1)) exp(-2n_r D(theta||1/2)) is finite for d>=2.
assumptions: for the weighted series only: d>=2, uniform ellipticity and s>=1 integer
entries.domain: probability, random walks in random environments

entries.title: Draft adaptive-center trap bound without false independence
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED SPECIAL-CASE CLAIM. Let the nearest-neighbor environment on Z^d have iid rows and every allowed transition at least kappa>0. B(x,r)=x+[-r,r]^d intersect Z^d, r an integer >=1; L=2r+1; n_r=r(2r+1)^(d-1); b_1(y)=omega(y,+e_1)-omega(y,-e_1). For delta>0, I_delta(x,r) counts rows in B with y_1<x_1 and b_1(y)>=delta, plus rows with y_1>x_1 and b_1(y)<=-delta. The plane y_1=x_1 is ignored. A_delta,theta(x,r)={I_delta(x,r)>=2 theta n_r}, theta in (1/2,1]. D(theta||1/2)=theta log(2theta)+(1-theta)log(2(1-theta)), with 0 log 0=0. For integer s>=1 put M_r(s)=2^s s! (2r+1)^s kappa^(-s(2r+1)). Let H be a genuine stopping time for the walk filtration enlarged by its entire fixed environment. Let C be an F_H-measurable integer center, with |C|_infinity<=N and X_H in B(C,r) on H<=N, for deterministic integer N>=0. Set Y equal to the exit time from that box measured after H and Y=0 on H>N. Then E_0[1_{H<=N}1_{A_delta,theta(C,r)}Y^s]<=M_r(s) min(1,(2N+1)^d exp(-2n_r D(theta||1/2))). Under Q=P_0(.|D^ell=infinity), q=P_0(D^ell=infinity)>0, where D^ell is first strict backtracking below the initial ell projection, this nonnegative moment is at most the same bound divided by q. Regeneration times cannot replace H because they depend on the future.
assumptions: H a stopping time with full environment included
q>0 only for the conditional-law extension

entries.title: Draft conditional renewal reduction to positive speed
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED CONDITIONAL REDUCTION. Suppose a nearest-neighbor walk is divided after a finite initial time into actual iid cycles, with integer durations S_i>=1 and displacements Z_i, satisfying |Z_i|_1<=S_i. If E[S_1]<infinity and E[Z_1 dot ell]>0, then X_n/n -> E[Z_1]/E[S_1] almost surely, with positive ell projection. The actual iid cycle law and its finite duration mean are explicit inputs, not consequences proved from C0041 in this packet.
entries.domain: probability, random walks in random environments

entries.title: C0041 hardest remaining input in the finite-trap route
entries.statement: UNPROVED INPUT. Under only iid, uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor RWRE on Z^d, d>=2, and annealed almost-sure transience in a fixed unit direction ell, show E_Q[tau_1]<infinity for Q=P_0(.|D^ell=infinity), D^ell first strict backtracking below the initial projection, and the standard time-valued directional regeneration tau_1=S_K at the first successful fresh-record attempt K. This is equivalent to summability of Q(tau_1>m). The present inward-box bounds do not classify arbitrary slow regions, excursions or repeated entries and cannot supply this input.
entries.domain: probability, random walks in random environments

entries.title: Draft radius-to-duration tail reduction without a stopping-time assumption
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED CONDITIONAL REDUCTION. For a UE nearest-neighbor walk started at 0, any almost surely finite positive integer-valued time tau (not necessarily a stopping time), and Q=P_0(.|E) with q=P_0(E)>0, put R=max_{0<=j<=tau}|X_j|_infinity. Then for integer r>=1,t>=0, Q(tau>t)<=Q(R>r)+q^(-1)(1-kappa^(2r+1))^floor(t/(2r+1)). If Q(R>r)<=C exp(-a r) for a>2log(1/kappa), then E_Q[tau]<infinity. This is an additional sufficient radius assumption, not a conclusion proved from directional transience.
assumptions: extra exponential radius tail only for the integrability conclusion

relations.rationale: The entropy calculation uses exactly the balanced row-density pattern defined here.
Only the weighted-moment series part uses the finite-box exit moment bound.
The deterministic-center union bound uses the precise inward-row entropy estimate.
The quenched stopping-time step uses the uniform finite-box moment estimate.
The missing finite cycle-duration mean is an explicit premise in this conditional positive-speed reduction.
This is an unproved sufficient input in the proposed route to the target; it is not a proof of the target.
The bounded-horizon adaptive estimate identifies why the passage to full regeneration integrability is still missing.
The fixed-box exit tail bound controls the time tail on the event of bounded path radius.
This is a proved conditional route to the missing duration mean; its radius premise is unproved from the target.
The existing dated C0041 card states exactly the UE iid directional-transience question; this draft records the still-unproved cycle-duration input for that same target.
